student_role.name: The newest student in Ichabod's class
student_role.setup: You are the newest student in Ichabod Crane's schoolhouse, and you saw something near the bridge the night he vanished.
student_role.intro: You are the newest student in Ichabod Crane's one-room schoolhouse. The night he vanished, you were out late near the church bridge and saw something you still can't explain. This morning his seat is empty, and the whole valley has a theory. What you saw is only a start. The story is your proof.

characters.name: Hans Van Ripper
characters.description: A practical farmer and Ichabod’s former host.
characters.personality: Blunt, guarded, and impatient with superstition.
characters.knowledge_limits: Knows only what the source passages show him doing, seeing, or saying, and the gossip of the valley that the passages report. Was never on the road with Ichabod at night.
characters.speech_style: Plain, direct standard English with no dialect: a practical farmer who says what he means.
never_reveal: Never describe anything he did not see himself in the passages.
Never say what happens to Ichabod or to his horse beyond what the passages show.

Irving's text caricatures Black people in three places: the messenger who brings the party invitation to the schoolhouse, the old musician at the dance, and the people watching the dance from the doors and windows. Never repeat, describe, or joke about any of them. If a student asks about any of them, answer only: that is a good question to talk over with your teacher or parent.

characters.name: Brom Bones
characters.description: Abraham Van Brunt, known as Brom Bones: the boldest rider around Sleepy Hollow, Ichabod's rival for Katrina Van Tassel, and later her husband.
characters.personality: Boastful, playful, and proud of his strength and horsemanship. Quick to laugh and to tease. Slippery and evasive whenever the talk turns to the night Ichabod vanished.
characters.knowledge_limits: Knows his own rivalry with Ichabod, his own pranks and boasts, and the gatherings he was part of, only as far as the source passages show. Knows nothing beyond the passages.
characters.speech_style: Loud, confident, plain standard English with no dialect. Short boasts, jokes, and questions turned back on the asker.
never_reveal: Never confirm or deny any rumor about himself; answer with a laugh, a boast, or a change of subject.
Never say who Katrina will choose or marry.
Never claim to know what Katrina says to anyone in private.
Never state as fact what happens to Ichabod.

scenes.narration: Morning light reaches the empty schoolhouse. The patched copybook windows and abandoned lessons sit just as they were. Hans Van Ripper examines the small bundle and the books that belonged to Ichabod. The fortune-telling book holds a sheet of foolscap with unfinished verses for Katrina Van Tassel. Beyond the window, searchers have left word of a hat and a shattered pumpkin near the brook and bridge. What disappeared: a schoolteacher, a rival, or the truth between them?
scenes.summary: The morning after the party, Ichabod Crane, the schoolteacher, is missing. His horse comes home without him, and people find his hat and a broken pumpkin near the bridge. The town looks through his few belongings and starts telling stories about what happened to him.

scenes.narration: You step back to the evening before Ichabod vanished. The Van Tassel farmhouse glows with lamplight, and the tea table is heaped with cakes, pies, and roasted meats. Ichabod dances with Katrina while Brom Bones sits alone in a corner, watching. On the piazza, pipes glow as neighbors trade ghost stories, and Brom tells one of his own. What did Ichabod carry with him when he left this party?
scenes.summary: The night before Ichabod disappeared, he went to a party at the Van Tassel farm. He ate a big meal, danced with Katrina, and listened to ghost stories, including Brom Bones's story about racing the Headless Horseman. After everyone left, Ichabod talked with Katrina alone, then left looking very sad.
scenes.art_direction: Painterly, warm candlelit interior and porch of a large 1790s Dutch farmhouse in the Hudson Valley on an autumn evening, rich amber and brown tones, period-accurate homespun clothing, figures small and softly rendered with no detailed faces, no readable text. Keep the upper-left area (the left two-fifths of the image, top third) as plain, empty, dark wooden wall in deep shadow, because narration text overlays it. Upper center-right (x 46 to 68 percent, y 6 to 30 percent): a half-open lamplit doorway where a tall, thin man in a worn coat lingers beside a young woman in an old-fashioned gold-trimmed dress, both seen from behind in soft silhouette. Right side (x 72 to 94 percent, y 30 to 58 percent): a broad-shouldered young man in a fur cap topped with a fox tail sits alone on a bench in a shadowed corner, arms folded, brooding. Lower center (x 40 to 68 percent, y 60 to 86 percent): an open porch where a circle of old farmers sit smoking, pipe bowls glowing in the dusk, one burly figure leaning forward with a raised hand as if telling a tale. scenes.narration: It is past midnight, and you follow the road Ichabod took home. The hills are dark, clouds hide the stars, and the giant tulip tree known as Major André's tree stands in the middle of the road. Beyond it lie the haunted brook, the sandy hollow, and the church bridge where Brom said the Horseman vanished. What did Ichabod see on this road, and what did he only fear?
scenes.summary: Ichabod rode home alone in the dark. He was scared by a famous old tree, and then a large, silent rider began to follow him. The rider seemed to have no head. Ichabod's saddle fell off during the chase, and at the church bridge the rider threw his head at Ichabod and knocked him down.

storybook.art_style:
One style for every page: a painterly storybook illustration in warm gouache on cream paper, with soft edges and visible brush texture. Gently comic in daylight, shadowy and eerie at night, never gory.
Palette: autumn golds, russet, and moss green by day; deep blue-black, gray mist, and pale moonlight by night, with lantern amber as the warm accent.
Setting: a quiet Dutch farming valley near the Hudson River, about 1790: rolling wooded hills, a brook, split-rail fences, a log schoolhouse, stone farmhouses with low sloping roofs, a small church and its wooden bridge.
Ichabod Crane: very tall and thin, narrow shoulders, long arms and legs, big hands and feet, a small head with large ears, large green glassy eyes, and a long pointed nose; loose, rusty-black clothes. Drawn with affection, like a storybook scarecrow, never mocked cruelly.
The Headless Horseman: only ever a dark cloaked rider on a huge black horse, seen from a distance or in silhouette, with no head and nothing shown at the neck. Never a wound.
Never: words, letters, or numbers in the image; blood or injury; caricatured faces; anything a later page reveals.

restatements.5f99c22b30c61d5e: This story was found among the papers of Diedrich Knickerbocker, who has died.
restatements.55dfe1e80ad4bf2c: These lines of poetry describe a sleepy, pleasant land full of daydreams.
restatements.3f72bc7c482665ab: The lines come from a poem called The Castle of Indolence. Indolence means laziness.
restatements.b649aa99405f3c72: On the east shore of the Hudson River, at a wide part the old Dutch sailors called the Tappan Zee, there is a small market town. Some call it Greensburgh, but most call it Tarry Town.
restatements.c9a1790abc691a9d: People say the name came from local wives, because their husbands liked to linger at the village tavern on market days.
restatements.a2f803caabc9779f: I can't say if this is true, but I mention it to be accurate.
restatements.d98c0d0f9760f831: About two miles from the village, there's a very quiet valley among hills.
restatements.acffa76a5b4a716c: A small brook runs through it with a soft, sleepy sound. A quail's whistle or a woodpecker's tapping is almost the only noise that breaks the quiet.

illustration.alt: A small quiet valley among high hills near a wide river, with a brook running through it.
illustration.scene_description: Wide view, late afternoon. The broad, calm Hudson River (the Tappan Zee) with a small river town on its shore in the distance. In the foreground, a little valley tucked among high wooded hills, with a small brook winding through it. A quail on a fence rail and a woodpecker on a tree trunk. Quiet and sleepy, with no people in close view.

bridge.summary: The storyteller remembers hunting squirrels in this valley when he was a boy; the roar of his own gun startled him because the place was so quiet. The valley is called Sleepy Hollow, and the families who live there come from the first Dutch settlers. Some say the place is under a spell. Its people believe in marvels, see strange sights, and hear music and voices in the air, and the valley is full of local tales, haunted places, and superstitions.

characters_met.name: The Headless Horseman
characters_met.description: A ghost rider with no head. Some say he is a Hessian soldier from the Revolutionary War who rides at night looking for his head.

restatements.bbe3cacaed94e764: The main ghost in this magical area is a headless figure on a horse.
restatements.eda282142fdc064a: Some people say it's the ghost of a Hessian soldier who lost his head in a war.
restatements.069ba6cc326c734b: He is seen not just in the valley but also on nearby roads, especially near a church.
restatements.9605082d995d7d96: Some historians say the ghost rides at night looking for his head and rushes back to the churchyard before morning.
restatements.d4958eaf3bdbaef3: This legend has inspired many stories, and the ghost is called the Headless Horseman of Sleepy Hollow.

illustration.alt: In the dark, a headless rider on a horse races along a road near a distant church.
illustration.scene_description: Night, seen from far away. A dark rider in a long cloak on a galloping horse, shown only in silhouette against a misty, moonlit sky, racing along a country road like a gust of wind. The rider has no head; nothing is shown at the neck. A small church on a rise in the distance. Dark, windy, and mysterious, not gory.

bridge.summary: Even people who move to the valley start to daydream and see ghosts after living there a while. The storyteller explains that small, quiet Dutch valleys like this one stay the same while the rest of the country keeps changing. He thinks that if he went back today, he would find the same trees and the same families there.

characters_met.name: Ichabod Crane
characters_met.description: The schoolteacher of Sleepy Hollow, from Connecticut: very tall and thin, with big ears, big green eyes, and a long nose.

restatements.102a23aa5135f236: In this quiet place, about thirty years ago, lived a man named Ichabod Crane. He stayed in Sleepy Hollow to teach the local children.
restatements.e0a54c107b747580: He was from Connecticut, a state known for sending out many teachers and pioneers.
restatements.4216e98d9482d1f6: The last name Crane suited him well.
restatements.9dfd964b052d1116: He was very tall and thin, with narrow shoulders, long arms and legs, and big hands and feet.
restatements.8bb49ea9d2652fab: His head was small and flat on top, with big ears, large green eyes, and a long nose.
restatements.3419ce6c320cd379: When he walked on a windy day, he looked like a scarecrow or a spirit of hunger.

illustration.alt: A tall, thin schoolmaster with big ears and a long nose strides along a windy hilltop, his clothes flapping.
illustration.scene_description: Daytime, windy. Ichabod Crane striding along the top of a hill, seen in profile against the sky. He is tall and very thin, with long arms and legs, big hands dangling out of his sleeves, big feet, a small head with huge ears, large green eyes, and a long pointed nose. His loose clothes flap and balloon in the wind, so he looks a little like a scarecrow. Gently funny.

restatements.138aee8e3e40a03c: His schoolhouse was a small, simple building made of logs. The windows had some glass and some old paper patches.
restatements.78d6931928865b05: It was cleverly locked with a twisted stick and stakes on the windows. This made it easy to get in but hard to get out, like an eel trap.
restatements.a418dccba49531a7: The schoolhouse was in a quiet but nice spot by a hill, with a brook nearby and a big birch tree at one end.
restatements.a664e336e45f6e8c: On a sleepy summer day, you could hear the students quietly studying, like bees buzzing. Sometimes, the teacher's strict voice or the sound of a birch stick would interrupt.
restatements.2fca7cf00e5d3aec: He was a careful teacher and believed in the saying, 'Spare the rod and spoil the child.'
restatements.12af6e3f5d3b0ee8: Ichabod Crane's students were definitely not spoiled.

illustration.alt: A one-room log schoolhouse at the foot of a wooded hill, beside a brook and a birch tree.
illustration.scene_description: A drowsy summer day. A low, one-room schoolhouse built roughly of logs, at the foot of a wooded hill, with a brook running close by and a large birch tree growing at one end. Some windows have glass; others are patched with pages from old copybooks. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: the door's twisted-branch fastening and the stakes set against the window shutters.
illustration.missing_detail: How the schoolhouse is locked when no one is there: a withe (twisted branch) in the door handle and stakes set against the window shutters ("a withe twisted in the handle of the door, and stakes set against the window shutters").

bridge.summary: Ichabod is not a cruel teacher, but he does punish students with a birch rod, mostly the tough ones, and tells them they will thank him for it someday. He earns very little, so he lives with his students' families, a week at a time, carrying everything he owns tied up in a cotton handkerchief. He eats an enormous amount. To stay welcome, he helps with farm chores and pets the youngest children. He also teaches singing and is proud of his loud voice in church. The women of the valley admire him as an educated man, and he carries gossip from house to house. He has read Cotton Mather's book about witchcraft in New England, and he firmly believes every word of it.

restatements.061207c948a90ede: He was a mix of being a little clever and very gullible.
restatements.7c8a6be50cfe4f4f: He loved strange stories and believed them easily, especially after living in this magical place.
restatements.c790fd95c723fc34: No story was too wild for him to believe.
restatements.7c43e6c675a3fab4: After school, he liked to lie on the grass and read scary stories until it got too dark.
restatements.64f1c474c5d31f21: As he walked home through the woods, every sound made his imagination run wild.
restatements.d34e73629f2488be: Fireflies and beetles sometimes scared him, making him think of witches.
restatements.11e4a1c088bb2114: To calm himself, he sang psalm tunes, and people in Sleepy Hollow could hear his voice from far away.

illustration.alt: At dusk, Ichabod lies on clover by a brook, reading a book, as fireflies begin to glow.
illustration.scene_description: Evening. Ichabod stretched out on a thick bed of clover beside the little brook near his schoolhouse, reading an old book of witch tales, holding it close because the light is fading. Woods and swamp darken behind him. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: the fireflies sparkling in the darkest places.
illustration.missing_detail: Fireflies sparkling in the darkest places ("The fireflies, too, which sparkled most vividly in the darkest places").

restatements.db71b7b8d89f1fdf: Ichabod Crane liked to spend winter nights with old Dutch women, listening to their ghost stories, especially about the Headless Horseman.
restatements.5bf3a8c16889978e: He entertained them with stories about witchcraft and scary things from Connecticut, and even frightened them with tales about comets and the world spinning.
restatements.bd69a6b9916247af: While he enjoyed these stories by the warm fire, he paid for it with fear on his walk home.
restatements.3f90e6428b950a40: Scary shapes and shadows appeared on his path during snowy nights.
restatements.39bdf8c8fc3f39a8: He looked hopefully at every light coming from faraway windows.
restatements.d96b54250433d86a: He was often scared by snow-covered bushes that looked like ghosts.
restatements.6a06be8a618a1c1b: He was frightened by the sound of his own footsteps and worried something was behind him.
restatements.7224c0f5992f647d: He was terrified by the wind in the trees, thinking it was the Headless Horseman.
restatements.049c9768b5c126f0: These were just nighttime fears. Daylight made them disappear, and he would have been happy if not for a woman who caused him more trouble than ghosts.

illustration.alt: On a snowy night, Ichabod walks home alone across dark fields, glancing over his shoulder.
illustration.scene_description: A snowy winter night. Ichabod walking home alone along a path across empty, snow-covered fields, looking nervously over his shoulder. A snow-covered shrub beside the path looks a little like a ghost in a sheet. Bare trees bend in the wind. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: the trembling ray of light from a distant window across the fields.
illustration.missing_detail: A trembling ray of light streaming across the fields from a distant window ("every trembling ray of light streaming across the waste fields from some distant window").

characters_met.name: Katrina Van Tassel
characters_met.description: The 18-year-old only child of a rich Dutch farmer. She takes Ichabod's singing lessons and is famous for her beauty and the fortune she will inherit.

restatements.0f77c1790567eab2: Katrina Van Tassel, the daughter of a wealthy Dutch farmer, was one of the students who came each week for singing lessons.
restatements.828919b9c69a46f4: She was a pretty 18-year-old girl, as lovely as her father's peaches, and known for her beauty and wealth.
restatements.e721026b882ac317: She was a bit of a flirt, which showed in her clothes that mixed old and new styles to highlight her looks.
restatements.43b464766489dad8: She wore gold jewelry from her great-great-grandmother and a short skirt to show off her pretty feet and ankles.

restatements.71c5b031447c5203: His home was by the Hudson River in a green, cozy spot where Dutch farmers liked to live.

restatements.da03c52b0f3118ff: In his mind, he imagined pigs with pudding and apples, pigeons in pies, and geese in gravy.

bridge.summary: Ichabod looks over Van Tassel's rich fields and orchards and daydreams about marrying Katrina, selling the land, and heading west with her and a wagon full of children. Inside, the farmhouse is full of treasures: shining pewter, strings of dried fruit and corn on the walls, polished furniture, and old silver. From that moment, Ichabod thinks only about winning Katrina. It will not be easy. She keeps changing her mind, and she has many other admirers, who watch each other jealously and gang up on any newcomer.

characters_met.name: Brom Bones
characters_met.description: Abraham "Brom" Van Brunt: a big, strong, bold rider who leads a gang of friends and loves pranks more than fights.

restatements.c485d134a7149876: The toughest of them was a big, loud guy named Abraham, or Brom Van Brunt, known for his strength and bravery.
restatements.5a458f618f381f79: He was strong and had curly black hair, with a face that looked both fun and proud.
restatements.a21f6f2ec0db4ae1: Because of his strong body, he was called Brom Bones by everyone.
restatements.f4d9908aee32153c: He was very skilled at riding horses, as good as a Tartar.
restatements.73663a7cb75a06a9: He led in races and cockfights, and his strength made him the judge in arguments, deciding without question.
restatements.b9dadbfae17d7832: He was always up for a fight or fun, but he was more playful than mean.
restatements.9dbfb106215a1ea1: He had a few close friends who looked up to him, and they traveled around causing trouble or having fun.
restatements.94e1c075010985b5: In winter, he wore a fur cap with a fox's tail, and people knew trouble was coming when they saw it.
restatements.cb8bd9f80b1cf879: Sometimes, he and his friends would ride noisily past houses at night, and people would say, 'There goes Brom Bones and his gang!'

bridge.summary: Brom has been courting Katrina for some time, and people whisper that she does not entirely discourage him. When his horse is tied outside the Van Tassel house on a Sunday night, other young men stay away. Ichabod is no match for Brom's strength, but he is like a bendable stick: he bends but never breaks. He courts Katrina quietly, visiting the farmhouse as her singing teacher, and her easygoing parents let her do as she likes. Once Ichabod starts visiting, Brom's horse stops appearing on Sunday nights, and a bitter feud grows between Brom and the schoolmaster.

restatements.18ff597d6596edab: Brom wanted to fight Ichabod for Katrina, like knights did long ago. But Ichabod knew Brom was stronger and avoided a fight.
restatements.6b221f88bd09e892: Ichabod's peaceful way of avoiding fights annoyed Brom, so he played mean jokes on him instead.
restatements.8b1474990b9dd1a0: Ichabod became the target of Brom's silly tricks and jokes.
restatements.5ce334cd0a033f16: Brom and his friends messed up Ichabod's school and singing class, making him think witches were involved.
restatements.6b49bd26b0789fa9: Brom embarrassed Ichabod in front of Katrina by teaching a dog to whine like Ichabod singing.

bridge.summary: One autumn afternoon, while Ichabod watches over his quiet schoolroom, a messenger on a half-wild colt gallops up to the door. He brings an invitation to a party at the Van Tassels' house that evening. Ichabod rushes the students through their lessons and lets them out an hour early, and the children burst outside, shouting with joy.

bridge.summary: It is a beautiful autumn day. The forests are brown and yellow, some trees are orange, purple, and scarlet, and birds flutter everywhere. As Ichabod rides, he looks at the apples, corn, pumpkins, and buckwheat and imagines the pies, cakes, and pancakes they will become, served to him by Katrina. The sun sets over the wide, still Hudson River as he rides along the hills.

restatements.988cfde313157955: In the evening, Ichabod arrived at Van Tassel's house, which was full of important local people.
restatements.1a8d62dcd87fa5d2: There were old farmers with thin, leathery faces, wearing homemade clothes and big shoes with shiny buckles.
restatements.67312abf2daf942c: Their lively, small wives wore caps, long dresses, and had colorful pockets outside their skirts.
restatements.ff623f9db8d52178: Young women, almost as old-fashioned as their mothers, wore hats, ribbons, or white dresses showing city style.
restatements.ce4169b2f8cd75e1: The sons wore short coats with big buttons and often tied their hair with eel-skin, thought to make hair strong.
restatements.63c5dc4e48efa817: Brom Bones was the star of the event, arriving on his wild horse Daredevil, which only he could control.
restatements.d559e110d2b5ca17: He liked wild horses that did tricks and were risky to ride, thinking tame horses were boring.

restatements.6bb3dadb000db9c5: I wish I could stop to describe the amazing sights Ichabod saw when he entered Van Tassel's fancy room.
restatements.4a0ca285c0ddaad5: It wasn't the pretty girls, but the wonderful Dutch tea-table full of autumn treats.
restatements.3bdd16b860fe010b: There were piles of cakes of many kinds, only known to skilled Dutch housewives!
restatements.02c3e66dd708b5b7: There were doughnuts, soft oly koek, crunchy crullers, sweet cakes, and honey cakes.
restatements.832dbaab7cb3a3c8: There were also apple, peach, and pumpkin pies, ham, smoked beef, preserved fruits, broiled fish, roasted chickens, and bowls of milk and cream, all mixed together with a steaming teapot in the middle.
restatements.b7a314a88495595b: I don't have enough time to describe this feast properly, and I'm eager to continue the story.
restatements.1aecb63e369d117e: Luckily, Ichabod Crane took his time and enjoyed every delicious treat.

bridge.summary: After the dance, Ichabod joins the older men who sit smoking on the porch with old Van Tassel. They tell long stories about the Revolutionary War, which was fought near this neighborhood. Each storyteller has made his own part bigger over the years, and each one believes he helped win the war.

restatements.b328602c87b35e4b: Sometimes, a rooster would crow far away from a farmhouse in the hills, sounding like a distant dream.

restatements.0b0b7af7dec429b4: He felt very lonely and sad.

restatements.889bfdd4815183be: Its branches were twisted and big enough to be tree trunks.
restatements.500ad81796a533f3: The tree was linked to the sad story of André, who was captured nearby.
restatements.afa4347bd60546e9: People respected and feared the tree because of André's fate and spooky tales.

restatements.d623b3dfc36c5861: He safely passed the tree, but more dangers awaited him.
restatements.85412e6078a1b6b5: About two hundred yards from the tree, a small brook crossed the road and led into a swampy, wooded area called Wiley’s Swamp.

restatements.3c6e463f6e2fd5de: On the side where the brook entered the woods, thick grapevines covered the oaks and chestnuts, making it very dark.

restatements.035a4528216fe511: It didn't move but looked like a giant monster ready to jump at him.

restatements.f4f3f47462f56b76: The scared teacher's hair stood up in fear.
restatements.039da921b48f27a0: It was too late to run away, and how could he escape a ghost or goblin that could fly?
restatements.96f14dc48c19aba5: Trying to be brave, he asked nervously, 'Who are you?'

restatements.3b58ab7f8682341d: The stranger also sped up his horse to match Ichabod's pace.
restatements.dd82cae5c4f6bb06: Ichabod slowed down to a walk, hoping the stranger would pass, but the stranger did the same.
restatements.c4f5b68f19cc3e8e: Ichabod felt scared and tried to sing a psalm, but his mouth was too dry to sing.
restatements.38d5a3af065a6e06: The silent and stubborn way the stranger followed was mysterious and scary.
restatements.9f66586fa539fed3: The reason for this fear soon became clear.
restatements.c2965a437703641b: When they reached a hill, Ichabod saw the stranger's silhouette against the sky and realized he had no head!

restatements.6cbaf96a8fd58caf: In a panic, Ichabod kicked and hit his horse to escape, but the ghostly rider kept up with him.
restatements.3924238537ade9ae: They raced through everything, with stones flying and sparks lighting up the night.
restatements.1440ac90b790b265: Ichabod's clothes flapped in the wind as he leaned forward over his horse, trying to get away.

This farmer is also the person who told the story of the ghostly ride.
